questions.title: What should you do if a dog moves your golf ball?
questions.question: You are playing golf and your ball is sitting still on the grass. A dog runs over and bumps your ball, and it rolls away. What should you do?

choices.text: Hit the ball from where the dog left it
Put the ball back where it was before the dog moved it, with no penalty
Put the ball back and add two shots to your score
Leave the ball and add one shot to your score

questions.explanation: If a dog (or something else not part of your game) moves your golf ball, you just put the ball back where it was before. You don’t get any penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots added to your score because of a mistake or breaking a rule.
The place where your ball was before it got moved.
Something or someone, like a dog, that is not playing golf with you, which changes how your ball is resting.

questions.teachingTip: You can remind children that animals or wind are outside influences and you just put your ball back if they move it.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they have to play the ball from where the dog left it.
Some may believe they get a penalty when an animal moves their ball.

questions.title: What to do if your ball is moved by a dog
questions.question: While playing from the fairway, a dog runs by and nudges your golf ball, moving it from its original spot. What is the correct action?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the dog moved it to
Place the ball back to its original spot with no penalty
Replace the ball and take a two-stroke penalty
Leave the ball and add a one-stroke penalty

questions.explanation: If an outside influence, such as a dog, moves your ball at rest, you must place the ball back in its original position without penalty.
